findings.title: import() calls in the object literal run eagerly, so nothing is lazy-loaded
findings.body: Every entry is `import("./x")`, and a dynamic import starts as soon as it is evaluated. All ~29 app modules therefore load when `@calcom/app-store` is first imported, so the cost is the same as the old static `import * as` and the lazy-loading benefit is lost. It also adds a failure mode: each promise is created up front and nobody awaits the ones that aren't used. If any single app module fails to import (missing optional dependency, bad env access at module scope), that promise rejects with no handler. That raises an unhandledRejection at startup (a process crash on Node 15+ defaults) even for code paths that never touch that app. The entries should be thunks, e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`, awaited per call site, so only the needed app loads and errors surface where it is used.

findings.title: async forEach callback makes the surrounding try/catch ineffective and leaves deletions un-awaited
findings.body: The callback is now `async` and awaits `getCalendar`. `forEach` ignores the returned promises, so the enclosing `try/catch` can no longer catch anything from `getCalendar` or `deleteEvent`. A failure, such as a CalendarService constructor throwing (which the old synchronous code would have caught and logged), becomes an unhandled promise rejection. The function also proceeds to send the reschedule email and `return true` before the calendar/video deletions have run. In a serverless handler the work can be cut off. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` (or a `for...of` loop with await) inside the try.

findings.title: async forEach callback makes the surrounding try/catch ineffective and leaves deletions un-awaited
findings.body: Same issue as in the vital app. `forEach(async ...)` with `await getCalendar(...)` means errors from `getCalendar`/`deleteEvent` bypass the `try/catch` and become unhandled rejections. The calendar and video deletions are not awaited before the email is sent and `true` is returned. Previously a synchronous throw from `getCalendar` would have been caught and logged. Replace with `await Promise.all(refs.map(...))` or a `for...of` loop.

findings.title: requestReschedule fires un-awaited async deletions with no error handling
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` now awaits `getCalendar` inside a fire-and-forget callback. Nothing awaits the calendar or video deletions, and any rejection from `getCalendar` or `deleteEvent` is an unhandled rejection that nothing logs. The mutation continues to send emails and webhooks and resolves before the previous calendar/video events are removed. In a serverless runtime the pending work may never finish. Collect the promises and `await Promise.all(...)` (with per-item error handling) before continuing.

findings.title: Recurring-cancel branch still uses async forEach, so deletions are neither awaited nor tracked in apiDeletes
findings.body: The PR converted the sibling legacy branch (lines ~477-483) from `forEach` to `for...of` with `await getCalendar`, so its promises land in `apiDeletes` before `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` runs. The recurring branch keeps `forEach(async ...)`. There, `apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent)` happens only after `await getCalendar(...)` and `await calendar.deleteEvent(...)`. By then `Promise.all` has already snapshotted `apiDeletes`, and the handler may have returned. The calendar events for the remaining recurring bookings are therefore not awaited and their errors are unhandled. Use a `for...of` loop (or `Promise.all` over `map`) so these deletions are actually part of `apiDeletes`. The `calendar` fetched at line 452 is also unused in this branch.
